topic: 1099-NEC/MISC threshold $2,000 for 2026 payments; W-9 now; due Feb 1, 2027; backup withholding exception (nov-push -> /1099-filing/)
label: 1099 season / Tip
headline: The 1099 line moved to *$2,000*

items.title: Under $2,000? No 1099-NEC
items.text: Up from $600, for payments made in 2026.

items.title: Get the W-9 now
items.text: Name, address and tax ID before the last payment.

items.title: Due Monday, Feb 1, 2027
items.text: To the contractor and the IRS. Jan 31 is a Sunday.

items.title: Withheld tax? File anyway
items.text: Backup withholding means a 1099, whatever the amount.

ig_caption:
Paid a contractor $1,500 this year? You may not need a 1099 for them anymore.

For payments made in 2026, the IRS reporting line for Form 1099-NEC (and 1099-MISC rents) moved from $600 to $2,000.

What to do before year-end:

1. Add up 2026 payments per contractor. $2,000 or more: a 1099-NEC is due. Under $2,000: generally no form.
2. Get a W-9 now, before the last payment, so you have the name, address and tax ID in January.
3. Mark the date: Monday, Feb 1, 2027. That's when the 1099-NEC goes to the contractor and the IRS (Jan 31 falls on a Sunday).
4. One exception: if you withheld backup tax because someone didn't give you a tax ID, you file a 1099-NEC no matter how small the payment.

Paid by card or PayPal? Those payments are reported by the payment company on a 1099-K, not by you on a 1099-NEC.

We prepare and e-file 1099-NEC and 1099-MISC forms for small businesses. Comment 1099 and we'll send the details.

Source: IRS Instructions for Forms 1099-MISC and 1099-NEC. General information, not tax advice.
